name: Tiroler Volkskunstmuseum
kurzbeschreibung: The Tiroler Volkskunstmuseum beside the Hofkirche is considered Europe's finest folk art museum: authentic wooden parlours, traditional costumes, and carnival masks.
beschreibung:
Overview

The renowned Tiroler Volkskunstmuseum in Innsbruck's historic old town is housed within the historic rooms of a former Franciscan monastery right next to the world-famous Hofkirche. In international specialist circles, it is regarded as one of the most fascinating and richest regional museums in Europe. Across three expansive floors, the museum presents an incomparable treasury of Alpine folk culture, rural craftsmanship, living customs, and historic domestic interiors from North, South, and East Tyrol as well as Trentino.

Collections & Historic Rooms

The museum was founded in 1888 on the initiative of a dedicated Tyrolean trade association to preserve the endangered artisanal cultural heritage of the Alpine region from oblivion; in 1929, it moved into its current magnificent premises in the Renaissance monastery arranged around an idyllic cloister. The undisputed highlight of the collection is the more than a dozen faithfully translocated farmhouse parlours (Stuben): dating from the 15th to 18th centuries from the valleys of Tyrol (Gothic, Renaissance, and Baroque), they were reassembled beam by beam inside the museum – including ornate coffered ceilings, tiled masonry stoves, and wood carvings. In addition, the museum houses a masterful collection of traditional Tyrolean costumes (Trachten), intricately carved nativity scenes (including the monumental Schöpfer-Krippe), hand-painted rustic furniture, pewter tableware, and wrought-iron guild signs. Another major attraction is the section dedicated to Alpine masking traditions, featuring archaic wooden masks and costumes from Krampus runs, Perchten, and famous Tyrolean carnival pageants such as the Schleicherlaufen.

Visit & Arrival

The Tiroler Volkskunstmuseum is open daily from 09:00 to 17:00 (last admission at 16:30). Admission prices (as of the 2025/2026 season): Regular €12.00 (includes entry to the adjacent Hofkirche with Emperor Maximilian I.'s "Schwarze Mander"), reduced €9.00, children and youths up to 19 years enjoy free admission. With the popular Innsbruck Card, entry is free. Arrival by train: From Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof, it is about a 10-minute walk through the city centre to Universitätsstraße 2. By public transport: Tram lines 1, 3 or city buses to the stop Museumstraße or Polizeidirektion. By car: Parking in the nearby underground City Garage or Markthallen-Garage.

Tips

The museum is largely barrier-free: a modern elevator serves all floors, and wheelchair-accessible restrooms are available (a few historic door thresholds in the translocated historic parlours may require minor assistance). Take advantage of the economical combined ticket to explore the adjacent Hofkirche immediately after your museum tour, home to the monumental cenotaph of Emperor Maximilian I. and its 28 larger-than-life bronze statues.
